repos.brief:
**What it does:** OmniRoute is an open-source TypeScript gateway that routes requests across 290+ AI providers (90+ free tiers) through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with quota-aware auto-fallback and token compression that can cut usage by 15–95%.

**Why now:** The project gained over 11,000 stars this week, signaling rapid community adoption, and its free-tier aggregation (~1.53B tokens/month from 43 provider pools) makes it immediately practical for builders hitting rate limits on individual providers.

**Build with it:** Drop it in front of Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, or any OpenAI-SDK client to get automatic failover across free tiers—useful for shipping AI-heavy apps or agents without paying for API access during development and early production.

**What it does:** Orca is an open-source Agent Development Environment (ADE) that lets you run multiple coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode) in parallel, each isolated in its own git worktree, with a Ghostty-class terminal, mobile companion app, and browser design mode for feeding UI context directly into prompts.

**Why now:** The repo spiked to 28,783 stars with 7,214 added this week, driven by growing demand for orchestrating fleets of AI coding agents rather than relying on a single sequential one—parallel agent workflows are becoming a practical productivity pattern.

**Build with it:** Fan a single feature prompt across five agents simultaneously, compare the resulting implementations across isolated worktrees, and merge the winner—cutting exploratory coding time dramatically on any TypeScript or multi-language codebase.

**What it does:** `code-review-graph` builds a persistent, Tree-sitter-parsed structural map of your codebase and exposes it via MCP, so AI coding tools pull only the relevant context for a given review rather than re-reading the entire repo—benchmarked at 38x–528x token reductions across real repositories.

**Why now:** The project is trending sharply this week (6,341 stars added), coinciding with growing frustration around runaway token costs in agentic Claude Code and Cursor workflows where large-repo reviews routinely exhaust context windows.

**Build with it:** Drop it into a CI pipeline via the provided GitHub Action to enforce graph-aware, low-token reviews on every PR, or wire the MCP server into your own LLM toolchain to give any agent precise, incremental code context without manual retrieval logic.

**What it does:** Agent Reach is a Python CLI that gives AI agents free, zero-configuration access to Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu, and more — routing around paywalls, rate limits, and login walls through a multi-backend fallback system.

**Why now:** It hit GitHub trending #1 this week with 60K+ stars and 3K new stars in seven days, partly because it just patched a live breakage (yt-dlp blocked by Bilibili's risk controls, silently rerouted to bili-cli) — demonstrating the maintenance model works under pressure.

**Build with it:** Drop `agent-reach` into any Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf workflow to give your agent real-time web research legs — scrape competitor Twitter threads, summarize YouTube tutorials, or monitor Reddit for bug reports, all without touching an API key or writing a scraper.

**What it does:** Dify is an open-source platform for building agentic workflows and RAG pipelines, combining LLM orchestration, a visual workflow editor, and tool integrations into a single deployable workspace that runs on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted infrastructure.

**Why now:** With 150,000+ stars and nearly 6,000 added this week alone, Dify just added MCP (Model Context Protocol) support, making it one of the fastest ways to wire real-world tools and data sources into production-ready AI agents.

**Build with it:** Deploy a self-hosted agent that connects your internal knowledge base via RAG, calls external APIs through MCP-compatible tools, and exposes a finished product endpoint—all without rebuilding the stack when you move from prototype to production.

**What it does:** UI UX Pro Max is a prompt-based AI skill (161 reasoning rules, 84 UI styles) that injects design system intelligence into coding assistants like Claude, Cursor, and Copilot, generating structured design systems, component hierarchies, and layout patterns from plain-language briefs.

**Why now:** With AI coding tools now capable of building full UIs from natural language, the bottleneck has shifted from code generation to design judgment — this fills that gap by giving those tools a repeatable, opinionated design layer rather than defaulting to generic output.

**Build with it:** Drop the skill into your AI editor of choice and build a production-ready landing page, mobile UI, or component library with consistent typography, spacing, and conversion-focused layout patterns generated before a single line of code is written.

**What it does:** Taste Skill is a collection of portable agent skills that inject opinionated layout, typography, spacing, and motion rules into AI coding agents like Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code, preventing them from producing generic-looking UIs. It also includes image-generation prompts for creating reference boards that can be handed directly to those agents for implementation.

**Why now:** With 2,677 stars added this week, it's hitting a nerve at the exact moment vibe-coding workflows are becoming mainstream and developers are frustrated that every AI-generated frontend looks identical. The timing aligns with rapid adoption of Claude Code and Codex as primary coding interfaces where design quality has become the obvious weak link.

**Build with it:** Drop the skills into your Claude Code or Cursor project, generate a reference board with ChatGPT Images using the included prompts, then build a polished SaaS dashboard or landing page where the AI actually respects visual hierarchy instead of defaulting to Tailwind boilerplate.

**What it does:** Awesome Claude Skills is a curated collection of 1,000+ reusable instruction packages ("skills") that extend Claude and other coding agents—Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI—with structured workflows for document processing, code tools, business automation, and app integrations via Composio's MCP Gateway.

**Why now:** The repo gained over 5,000 stars this week, signaling a surge in developer interest in packaging agent behavior as portable, version-controlled skill files rather than one-off prompts.

**Build with it:** Drop a `SKILL.md` into your Claude Code setup to give your agent repeatable, shareable workflows—then connect it to the Composio MCP Gateway to trigger real actions across 1,000+ apps like GitHub, Slack, and Gmail with built-in auth handling.

**What it does:** Graphify turns any codebase—plus its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs—into a queryable knowledge graph using local, deterministic tree-sitter AST parsing, with every graph edge labeled as either directly extracted or inferred so you know exactly what the tool read versus reasoned. It integrates as a `/graphify` slash command inside Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI, replacing grep-based code search with structured graph queries.

**Why now:** The project gained nearly 5,000 stars this week, signaling a surge of developer interest likely tied to the rapid adoption of Claude Code and Gemini CLI as primary coding environments where deep codebase understanding is a bottleneck. Its MCP and skills integrations position it squarely in the current wave of tool-augmented AI coding agents.

**Build with it:** A builder could use Graphify to power a code review agent that traverses call graphs and dependency edges to surface ripple effects of a proposed change before a PR is merged. It's also a strong foundation for a legacy codebase onboarding tool that lets new engineers query relationships across undocumented SQL schemas, configs, and source files in plain language.

**What it does:** Ponytail is a JavaScript plugin for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that enforces YAGNI discipline—replacing over-engineered solutions with minimal alternatives, averaging 54% fewer lines of code across real agentic sessions on a production FastAPI + React codebase.

**Why now:** It's trending at 89K+ stars with 3,794 added this week, likely surfing the wave of developers frustrated with Claude Code burning tokens on unnecessary abstractions and dependencies during the current agentic coding boom.

**Build with it:** Drop ponytail into your Claude Code or Cursor workflow to cut AI-generated boilerplate on your next feature sprint—particularly effective if you're scaffolding CRUD APIs or React UIs where agents habitually over-install packages.
